search.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Measurements were made on amino acid contents in collection of wild barley (<jats:italic>Hordeum spontaneum</jats:italic>)., grown in pot conditions, and in some Israeli breeding lines and cultivars of <jats:italic>Hordeum vulgare. H. spontaneum</jats:italic> was low in lysine content and high in prolilne plus glutamic acid compared to <jats:italic>H. vulgare.</jats:italic> Lysine content was positively correlated, in H. <jats:italic>spontaneum</jats:italic>, to all other ammo acids except proline and giutamic acid. Inter‐populanon rnean differences for Iv‐saie in <jats:italic>H. spontaneum</jats:italic> were small and lysine variation was obscured due to variation in protein content.</jats:p><jats:p>The use of <jats:italic>H. spomancum</jats:italic> in breeding high protein. nutritionally improved barley is discussed.</jats:p>
title: Amino Acid Resources of the Wild Relative of Barley (Hordeum spontaneum) in Israel
